about: Data brokers and how to get off each one. Public company details only, no personal data. Researched and cross-checked against live sites on the date in each entry; opt-out pages change often, so re-check anything older than a few months.

brokers.name: ANA Email Preference Service (eMPS)
brokers.notes:
Free ('There is no charge to register for eMPS') and lasts 10 years, after which you must register again. The only field is the email address.

ANA emails a verification CODE, not a link, to each address. It must be entered on the next page within 60 minutes or the address is removed. The email-link enum is the closest fit. The page sets no limit on the number of addresses.

It removes the address from the national US email lists of marketers that use eMPS only. No effect on non-users, B2B email at work, or non-US senders. The page shares the registration with participating companies; pressing CANCEL aborts it.

brokers.name: California DROP (Delete Request and Opt-out Platform)
brokers.notes:
Use this first if the owner lives in California. One free request goes to every broker registered with the CPPA. The 2026 registry CSV has 603 broker rows, which I re-counted, and the state says 'over 600'. It does NOT reach unregistered brokers. Only California residents can use it. You may file for another CA resident (a child or an elderly relative) with their authorisation, but one request may cover only one person (portal Terms of Use).

What the form asks for: how-drop-works says the deletion request needs only name, date of birth and ZIP. Email, phone, MAID, connected-TV ID and VIN are optional and improve matching. You can add multiples of everything except DOB. The Markup (Jan 2026) reports a cap of 3 ZIPs, 3 emails and 3 phones. The portal Terms of Use say you will be prompted for 'name, date of birth, and email address', and that 'certain information is required to verify your residency'.

Residency check: it runs through the California Identity Gateway (vendors Socure and Login.gov) and has two routes. You cannot switch after choosing.
- Manual route: The Markup says it uses phone, email, California address or SSN. Each email or phone must be confirmed with a single-use code before you submit. The code is entered, not clicked; the email-link enum is the closest fit.
- Login.gov route: needs an account and uploaded photos of a government ID, so it is an ID-DOCUMENT route. Avoid it if possible.
FLAG: official pages never mention SSN; The Markup lists it as a possible Gateway input. Leave it blank. If verification fails, you can request a residency review, answered by email.

After you submit, you get an 8-digit DROP ID. Check status at https://consumer.drop.privacy.ca.gov/dropstatus and recover a lost ID at https://consumer.drop.privacy.ca.gov/id_recovery. You can update your profile once every 45 days.

Broker obligations: since 2026-08-01 brokers must pull DROP at least every 45 days. They must report a status within 90 days: Deleted, Exempted, Opted-out (no exact match, so the broker keeps the data but may not sell or share it), Record not found, or Pending. They must keep deleting newly collected matches every 45 days. The request stays active ('DROP is ongoing'), so there is no need to resubmit.

All active and future brokers are included by default. You can untick specific brokers on the data broker list page inside DROP. Exempt data, including public records, may be kept. Penalty per CalPrivacy: $200 per consumer per day for a broker that misses the 45-day pull. Requests filed before 2026-08-01 sat as Pending until then.

This is an interactive state portal with identity proofing. The tool should send the owner there, not automate it.

brokers.name: DMAchoice (ANA mail preference service)
brokers.notes:
FLAG, PAYMENT: $8 online (card or PayPal) or $9 by mail (check or money order payable to ANA; no cash, certified or registered mail), for 10 years. I confirmed this on register.php and in the FAQ. Older guides quoting $2-$7 are stale (the FTC 2022 page still says $6/$7).

Registration creates an account. Email is the username. The password needs 8+ characters with a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter, a digit and a special character.

Required fields: first name, last name, address, city, state, ZIP, email (entered twice) and phone. No DOB. You can add up to 4 extra name versions and 4 extra addresses (5 records per household). You pick mail categories.

Allow 90 days for it to take effect (FAQ). It only stops 'prospect' mail from companies that use the ANA suppression file. It does not stop:
- transactional mail
- mail from companies you have bought from, subscribed to or donated to
- political mail
- 'current resident' (EDDM) mail
- non-member senders
- prescreened credit offers (use OptOutPrescreen)

Mail-in: DMAchoice, Consumer Preferences, P.O. Box 900, Cos Cob, CT 06807 (form at https://www.dmachoice.org/prefill_mailin_registration.php).

The same site links the free Deceased Do Not Contact and Caretaker lists, which are not relevant to the owner.

brokers.name: Google Results about you
brokers.notes:
Removes results from Google Search only. The broker's page stays up ('it doesn't mean that the info is gone from the internet'). It is still useful for finding which people-search sites list the owner.

Who can use it: you need a signed-in Google account and must be 18+ 'in certain markets'. The help page lists no countries. Minors use a separate form.

What you enter: your name, plus only the contact details you want watched (home address, phone, email; several of each allowed; nicknames and maiden names optional). Address, phone and email are each optional individually; supply only what the owner wants monitored.

Alerts: Google notifies you of matching results 'within a few hours', by email or in the Google app. You then request removal per result; the confirmation arrives within hours, and removal shows a few hours after approval.

FLAG: since 2026-02-10 (US rollout) you can also add government ID numbers (SSN, driver's licence, passport) to be watched. These are optional; the tool should not supply them. The sources do not say whether a partial number is accepted.

Not covered: government, education, news and business sites, and content you control yourself. To stop monitoring, go to Settings > 'Remove all personal info'.

brokers.name: National Do Not Call Registry
brokers.notes:
Not deletion. It stops telemarketing sales calls, not data collection. Free and never expires ('Registrations ... DO NOT EXPIRE'). A number is removed only if it is disconnected and reassigned, or on request.

Online registration takes up to three phone numbers plus an email address (entered twice) in three steps. The email is used only to confirm. Register@donotcall.gov sends one email per number, and you must click each link within 72 hours. I read these steps from the site's own en-US.json strings, because register.html is a jQuery shell.

Alternatively, call 1-888-382-1222 (TTY 1-866-290-4236) from the number being registered; no email is needed that way.

The number appears on the Registry the next day, but sales calls can take up to 31 days to stop. Not covered: scam calls, business and fax numbers, and political, charity, debt-collection, informational and survey calls.

Pennsylvania and Wyoming residents can also join their state lists through ANA's Telephone Preference Service (https://www.ims-dm.com/cgi/dnclist_form.php). The FTC FAQ is dated Sept 2023.

brokers.name: OptOutPrescreen.com (prescreened credit and insurance offers)
brokers.owner: Nationwide consumer credit reporting companies (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion, Innovis)
brokers.notes:
One request removes you from the prescreen marketing lists of all four bureaus. It is not deletion and does not stop other junk mail.

How to opt out:
- Online, for 5 years.
- By phone: 1-888-5-OPT-OUT (1-888-567-8688). The phone line also asks for your home phone.
- Permanent: start online or by phone, then sign and mail the 'Permanent Opt-Out Election' form (older Experian wording: 'Notice of Election to Opt Out'). SIGNATURE, permanent route only. Print the form from the confirmation page, or get it by mail if you started by phone. Mail it to Opt-Out Department, P.O. Box 530200, Atlanta, GA 30353 (address per Experian and a Sept-2026 guide).

FLAG: the form also asks for SSN/ITIN and date of birth. The FTC (2022) and guides quoting the site say both are optional ('If you leave them blank, we will attempt to process your request without this information'). The tool should leave them blank. Reported 15-minute time limit to finish the form.

Experian says it takes effect within 5 days, but offers can keep coming for up to 60 days or longer.

Access: every path I tried (/, /form, bare domain) returned 403 to both curl and WebFetch, so I could not read the form myself. A Sept-2026 guide (redact.dev) says the site only responds to US internet connections, which may explain the block. Fields come from Experian, the FTC and 2026 guides. There may be a deep link at https://optoutprescreen.com/form (seen in search results), but I could not load it. The home page link 'Click here to opt-in or opt-out' is the reliable start.

brokers.name: AdvancedBackgroundChecks
brokers.notes: Same company as FastPeopleSearch and its sister sites. Its 2026 California filing says a do-not-sell request on one site applies to all of them, but listing removal is per site, so file here too, then re-check the sisters a few days later. Loaded live 2026-10-08 with WebFetch; curl still gets a 403. The site now uses the two-stage MTA form. Stage 1 asks for subject or agent, first, middle (optional) and last name, email, consent and reCAPTCHA. The emailed link expires in 24h. The page says 'Depending on your state of residence, you may have the right...' and promises a results email 'within 45 days of submission'. Stage 2 (Redact, May 2026): first and last name, city, state, ZIP and email are required; middle name, DOB, phone and street are optional; then a review box and CAPTCHA. The confirmation says '3 days or less'. Redact's /removal URL returns 404, so /opt-out is correct. BADBOOL dropped this site on 2026-09-27 because its opt-out 'no longer works in all states', so expect a denial outside comprehensive-privacy-law states.

brokers.name: Ancestry.com (searchable record indexes)
brokers.notes: FLAG for owner decision: per BADBOOL you must create a FREE Ancestry account (not a free trial) to find the record URLs. That conflicts with the tool's no-account rule. Checked live 2026-10-08: the Privacy Center gives privacy@ancestry.com (decoded from a protected link). The 'Requesting Content Removal' help article points to the report-issue form, which support.ancestry.com/s/reportissue now 307-redirects to. On that form, pick 'Sensitive information about my living family is displayed' or 'Privacy'; it cannot be used on behalf of others, and I could not tell whether it needs a login. You can also click 'Report a problem' on any record page. BADBOOL route: email privacy@ancestry.com the record URLs for every state you have lived in. Privacy statement: removal from searchable indexes is 'case-by-case'; linked archival records must go to the archive itself. FLAG: for U.S. access/deletion requests Ancestry 'may' require a copy of a government ID. Archives.com is a separate removal (already on the list). Ancestry dropped its footer 'Do Not Sell or Share' link around May 2026 (ConductAtlas).

brokers.name: Archives.com (living-person search)
brokers.notes: Checked live 2026-10-08: /Optout 301-redirects to /optout ('Opt-Out Request Form'). It suppresses your info from Archives.com living-person search results only. About the person: First Name*, Last Name* and Address 1* required; Middle Name, Address 2/3, Phone and Email optional, so omit them. About the requester ('Same as above' checkbox available): First and Last Name*, Email* and Confirm Email*. A required 'Additional Information' box asks you to describe the records and search criteria used. Agree to the Opt-Out Policy and solve the CAPTCHA (reCAPTCHA). An email confirmation comes once records are identified and suppressed, typically within 30 days. Opting out does not affect any subscription or billing. No account needed (searching itself needs a free trial; cancel it). Does not cover Ancestry.com, Fold3 or Newspapers.com. Ancestry ownership is not stated on the page ('© 2026 Archives').

brokers.name: BackgroundCheckers
brokers.notes: CHANGED: on 2026-10-08 this domain serves the same optOutLight form as its siblings (name, full DOB, city, ZIP, state, email, then a confirmation link; phone (833) 714-0641). redact.dev (tested 2026-08-11, updated 2026-09-22) said the old footer form failed on unreadable CAPTCHAs and recommended a written request to support@privaterecords.net, the registry contact. That advice now looks superseded, but no submission was tested. Separate request from the other Private Records LLC sites.

brokers.name: BeenVerified
brokers.owner: The Lifetime Value Co. (LTVCO), via BeenVerified, LLC
brokers.notes: Checked live 2026-10-08: /app/optout/search and /optout both 301-redirect to /svc/optout/search/. That page is Cloudflare-blocked to bots, so the fields come from guides. Flow (DeleteMe updated 2026-09-15 and verified Aug 2026; Clearnym Aug 2026): search by name and state, 'Proceed to Opt Out', enter email, hCaptcha, then click 'Verify Opt-Out' in the email; a second email confirms. CONFLICT: redact.dev (May 2026) reached a 'Do Not Sell' identity form marking age, street address, city, state and ZIP as required. Send those only if the live form demands them. BeenVerified's privacy policy (updated 09/09/2026, checked live) says you may also email privacy@beenverified.com, use its online request form, or phone or mail to opt out Public information. ccpa@beenverified.com is guide-reported. ReversePhone.com's footer 'Do Not Sell or Share' link points to this BeenVerified opt-out (checked live). ReversePhone is therefore listed in covers, by inference. NumberGuru's footer link also points here, but NumberGuru has its own path too; file both. Other LTVCO brands (PeopleLooker, PeopleSmart, NeighborWho, Ownerly) each run their own opt-out and privacy@ address, so file them separately. Typical 24-72h. Re-listing after moves is reported. ReversePhone.com is a BeenVerified, LLC site, but it's not confirmed that this request removes it; check it afterwards.

brokers.name: CheckPeople
brokers.notes: ASKS FOR DATE OF BIRTH. Checked live 2026-10-08: 'Suppression Center' page with a required email field and a terms/consent checkbox. 'Upon submission of your email address you will receive a verification email with a link to proceed.' The wording is identical to PeopleConnect's Suppression Center, so expect the same behaviour, possibly including rejection of alias/disposable emails. After the link (per redact.dev, Aug and Oct 2026): DOB, which cannot be changed, then legal first, middle and last name, then match and suppress records. CheckPeople says 5-7 days. checkpeople.com/optout 301-redirects to /privacy-rights (checked). Sister site UnMask (unmask.com/opt-out/) uses CheckPeople data but needs its own request. Contacts: support@checkpeople.com and 1-800-267-2122 (on the page); compliance@checkpeople.com if no record is found (guide-reported). California residents can use the state's DROP platform for deletion.

brokers.name: CheckSecrets (Truth Now LLC)
brokers.notes: Checked live 2026-10-08: same optOutLight template (name, full DOB, city, ZIP, state, email, then a confirmation link). Phone (855) 754-7951; registry contact support@checksecrets.com. The page has template glitches (duplicated sections, a blank date in the 'already confirmed' text). Earlier reports said this form was broken; whether submissions work now is untested. The CA registry lists peoplesearchusa.org, sealedrecords.net and 'inmatesearcher.com' under Truth Now LLC, each with a separate form.

brokers.name: Classmates.com
brokers.notes: classmates.com and help.classmates.com returned 403 / Cloudflare challenge to me on 2026-10-08. The PeopleConnect Suppression Center's live terms state it does not apply to Classmates.com, so this separate route is needed. Alumni listing (redact.dev, walked 2026-08-25): find your page (classmates.com/people/...) by browsing state, town, school and alumni list. Submit the support form, choosing 'Edit Personal Information', with email, name and subject, and put the listing URL in Description, explicitly asking for deletion. No account needed; do not register. Classmates may email to confirm identity; send only the minimum. Yearbook photos: email privacy@classmates.com with name as printed, school, year and page. Do not pay to find the page. The support form and the privacy@ address are separate queues. No stated timeline ('reasonable time'); follow up after 2 weeks.

brokers.name: Clustal (clustal.org people-search)
brokers.notes: Returned 403 to WebFetch on 2026-10-08 (homepage and /privacy-control/), so nothing here was checked live. Flow per BADBOOL (updated 2026-09-27) and PrivacyOn (2026): search the site, open 'view full record' and copy that URL (the search-result URL does not work), paste it into /privacy-control/ with an email, then click the emailed confirmation link. PrivacyOn says links often expire within 24h. BADBOOL: each listing needs a DIFFERENT email address. Sources disagree on the support address: Optery lists help@clustal.org and PrivacyOn lists support@clustal.org. Neither is needed for the web flow. PrivacyOn's suggestion to give your full name as shown on the listing is not part of the BADBOOL flow, so send only URL plus email. Ownership is unknown. Possible siblings unpan.org and everyjoe.com use the same URL-plus-email flow but are not confirmed to share an operator (separate entries). BADBOOL marks it crucial; Optery lists it as Core.

brokers.name: CocoFinder
brokers.notes: I could not verify this. The site returns a Cloudflare 403 to both curl and WebFetch, and no 2026 source walked the form. Search by name and state and copy your profile URL. Sources disagree on the form: Incogni (updated Nov 2022) says remove-my-info links to a Google Docs form with first name, last name, email, record URL and a message, and no verification step; mePrism (2026, generic template) says name, email and URL with an email verification link and 24-72h. Offlist (updated 2026-08-13) says the fields aren't published, no SLA is confirmed, and support@cocofinder.com is the published fallback. Requests made for someone else need written authorization. Use a masked email. Re-lists over time; recheck every 6-12 months.

brokers.name: CyberBackgroundChecks
brokers.notes: Same company as FastPeopleSearch and its sister sites. Its 2026 California filing says a do-not-sell request on one site applies to all of them, but listing removal is per site, so file here too, then re-check the sisters a few days later. Form 1 (Redact May 2026, DeleteMe 2026-09-14): first, middle (optional) and last name, email, consent box and reCAPTCHA, then 'Send Request'. The email from support@cyberbackgroundchecks.com ('Complete your cyberbackgroundchecks.com Privacy Request') has a link valid for 24h. Form 2, the 'Record Suppression Form', prefills name and email. Street address, city and state are required; phone and DOB are not marked required (DeleteMe: phone 'not mandatory'). No ZIP is documented. Leave special characters out of name fields ('Brown Jr', not 'Brown, Jr.'). Removal takes 3 days or less. A California-only CCPA route also exists (older guides cite /ccparemoval) but isn't needed. The site returns a Cloudflare 403 to automated fetch.

brokers.name: EveryJoe
brokers.notes: Homepage and /do-not-sell/ both returned 403 on 2026-10-08. BADBOOL added it in Sept 2026: find your record, copy the link, paste it on the opt-out page. A OneRep guide (June 2026), which I saw only as a search summary because the page was 403, describes the same flow: footer 'Do Not Sell My Info' pre-filled with the profile URL, then your email, then a 'Delete my info' button in the verification email. It also mentions an email-support fallback, but I found no address. A link to Clustal or unpan is unconfirmed.

brokers.name: FamilyTreeNow
brokers.notes: Two-stage 'Privacy Request' flow (Redact, May 2026). Form 1: 'I am requesting as' (the person), first and last name (middle optional), email, consent box and hCaptcha, then 'Begin Privacy Request'. The single-use emailed link expires in 24h and opens a second form asking for 'additional verification info' to match the listing. Its fields aren't documented; expect location and/or DOB, as older guides used name, city/state and birth year. The confirmation says 3 days or less. Skip the affiliate 'Remove My Personal Data From 300+ Other Sites' button. DeleteMe (Sept 2026) still describes the older search and 'Opt Out This Record' flow. Re-lists over time. The 2026 CA registry lists Family Tree Now, LLC with privacy@familytreenow.com and 877-838-4889. The site returns a Cloudflare 403 to automated fetch.

brokers.name: FastBackgroundCheck
brokers.notes: Same company as FastPeopleSearch and its sister sites. Its 2026 California filing says a do-not-sell request on one site applies to all of them, but listing removal is per site, so file here too, then re-check the sisters a few days later. COVERED by the MTA network request (see fastpeoplesearch). Redact (2026-08-05) cites the operator's filing that the record-level opt-out 'travels across all ten sites', which matches the 2026 CA registry text. Form 1 (DeleteMe, updated 2026-09-22, 'as of May 2026'): subject or agent, name, email, agreement box and reCAPTCHA. The emailed 'Click here to fill out the form' link opens Form 2, an almost identical form with fields matching the listing. Its fields aren't itemized; MTA siblings ask for city, state, ZIP and street or DOB. Removal takes '3 days or less'. DeleteMe says it rejects opt-outs from states without a comprehensive privacy law. The site returns a Cloudflare 403 to automated fetch.

brokers.name: FastPeopleSearch
brokers.notes: Same company as FastPeopleSearch and its sister sites. Its 2026 California filing says a do-not-sell request on one site applies to all of them, but listing removal is per site, so file here too, then re-check the sisters a few days later. Checked live 2026-10-08: the page loaded as 'Do Not Sell/Right to Opt-out'. Step 1: 'I am' (subject or authorized agent), First Name*, Middle Name (optional), Last Name*, Email address*, authorization checkbox, and a Cloudflare Turnstile captcha. The emailed link must be used within 24h. Step 2 (redact.dev, May 2026): name, city, state and ZIP required, plus EITHER date of birth OR street address. Prefer street address over DOB for minimisation. Phone and email are also shown; leave phone blank unless forced. 'Please allow 3 days.' The page footer links a partner API (EnformionGO). USPhoneBook and PeopleSearchNow share the operator but are not confirmed covered; file separately. The Big-Ass list marks it high-risk. search_url left null: /search?name=... returns 404, and /name/... pages are bot-blocked, so no pattern could be confirmed.

brokers.name: Find People Fast
brokers.notes: Only CrabClear (2026-07-26) gives this route, and it could not view the form because of a Cloudflare challenge. I also got a 403 on 2026-10-08. Described flow: find your record, copy the full profile URL, submit it with your email (plus any CAPTCHA or consent step), then confirm via the emailed link. No official timeline; third parties estimate 24-48h or 3-7 business days. The operator is not named. This is a different site from FastPeopleSearch (MTA).

brokers.name: IDCrawl
brokers.notes: Aggregates social profiles, usernames and people-search data. Submit the exact profile URL (with https://, not a search-results page) plus an email, pass the CAPTCHA, then click the verification link (PrivacyOn, 2026-07-06; CrabClear loaded the form in headed Chrome on 2026-07-01). Each URL needs its own request; also check old cities and usernames. Takes 5-7 business days, up to 2 weeks. Email support@idcrawl.com if it's still up after 14 days. The site returns a bot challenge (HTTP 202/403) to automated fetch.

brokers.name: Inforver
brokers.notes: UNREACHABLE on 2026-10-08: SERVFAIL on Google and Cloudflare DNS, with its Google-hosted name servers refusing the query. CrabClear found it live on 2026-07-26 with 'Remove my info' / 'Do Not Sell My Info' links, so this may be recent or temporary; no other source reports a shutdown. Last-known flow: copy your profile URL (or use 'CONTROL PROFILE'), enter name, email and URL, pass the CAPTCHA, then verify by email. Inforver claims deletion within 3 business days. CrabClear notes the privacy route sometimes redirected to the homepage; don't submit anywhere off inforver.com. DeleteMe's /control/after_request?rid= URL is session-specific. Recheck before sending.

brokers.name: InfoTracer
brokers.notes: METHOD CHANGED TO EMAIL (checked live 2026-10-08). infotracer.com/optout/ is now a 'Your Privacy Choices' page with no search/removal form; the old name-plus-state 'Remove Data' tool is gone. Its 'Do Not Sell or Share' page says: to have your information removed from search results, email privacy@infotracer.com and 'include your first name, last name, state, and city'. Each record must be submitted separately. If you asked for a confirmation and have none within 15 days, follow up at the same address. Sending the email necessarily discloses your email address. The page also links a TrustArc rights-request form (submit-irm.trustarc.com) for access/deletion, answered within 45 days, which may ask more questions to verify identity. It lists those rights for residents of 19 privacy-law states, while the email removal route is not state-limited. Covered persons (judges, police) use subject 'Attention Covered Person Removal Request'. Sibling InfoPay/Accucom sites (CourtCaseFinder, StateCourts.org, ThePublicIndex, CourtRecords.us, StateRecords, RecordsFinder) each need their own request. No ID or payment.

brokers.name: InmatesSearcher
brokers.notes: Checked live 2026-10-08 at inmatessearcher.com (double s): same optOutLight template, phone (855) 512-1119. The CA registry spells it 'inmatesearcher.com' (single s), but that domain served a different page ('Inmate Searcher') with no optOutLight form, so the registry entry is probably a typo. Separate request from the other Truth Now sites.

brokers.name: Kids Live Safe
brokers.notes: Checked live 2026-10-08. Same white-label form (name, city, state, ZIP, age, email, human check; email-link confirmation, and 'Delete' requires an email reply). Phone 1-800-301-5905. Separate removal from quickpublicrecords.com despite the shared owner.

brokers.name: LocateFamily
brokers.notes: locate.family is NXDOMAIN; the real site is locatefamily.com, which resolves (Cloudflare) but returns a 403 to curl and WebFetch. It is a worldwide address directory: Trustpilot reviewers are in the US, Canada, the UK, Australia and several EU countries. DeleteMe (2026-09-14): browse by letter rather than search. Listings with a trash-can icon link straight to an opt-out form. Otherwise copy the listing URL, note the number beside your name, and submit both with your details at removal2.html; you may need to confirm by email. A Jul 2025 reviewer says the form requires full name, email and phone, so phone is included here (unverified). WARNING: 2022-2024 reviews report requests for an ID scan, a phone bill or proof of address, mostly outside the US. Don't send ID unless the live form demands it. Timing is unclear; mePrism (2026, generic) says 3-10 business days, and reviewers report anything from 24-48h to weeks, refusals and re-listing.

brokers.name: Men Stopping Violence (people-search on a former nonprofit's domain)
brokers.notes: 403 on 2026-10-08. Per redact.dev (walked through 2026-08-11): search your name, click VIEW FULL PROFILE (not VIEW CRIMINAL RECORDS, which is a Truthfinder ad), and copy the /people/<name>/<id>/ URL. Paste it into the Profile Link field, then REMOVE MY INFO, then confirm the record and enter your email, then CONFIRM & CONTINUE. Finish with COMPLETE REMOVAL in the email from info@menstoppingviolence.org; the link is single-use. Disposable email domains are rejected. Optery gives /privacy/ as the URL; BADBOOL and redact use /opt-out/. Optery notes 'some users have reported that the site's opt-out function is ineffective', so recheck after a few days. Same code as nationalpublicdata.com, but removals do not carry over and each site needs its own request. Operator is anonymous. BADBOOL marks it crucial.

brokers.name: MugshotLook
brokers.notes: Checked live 2026-10-08: same optOutLight template (name, full DOB, city, ZIP, state, email, then a confirmation link). Phone (888) 408-3417. Separate request.

brokers.name: MyLife
brokers.notes: BIRTH YEAR ONLY (YYYY), not a full date of birth: the tool should send just the year. RecordingLaw (field-by-field audit 2026-08-14) lists as required: State, First and Last Name, City, Postal/ZIP, Email Validator ('Verify Email' button) and Birth Year ('Your birth year helps us locate your correct profile'), plus reCAPTCHA. Optional: Middle Initial, Maiden/Alias Name, and Profile URL. Offlist (checked 2026-09-02) also says birth year is required but treats email as optional. The profile URL is optional, so you need not find your listing first. Email verification is an emailed code or validation step, not a click-through link (redact.dev). The form says requests are processed 'within the legally required time frames'; users report 1 day to about 15 business days. ID WARNING: the Big-Ass list reports MyLife sometimes asked for an account and a driver's license; no 2026 walkthrough saw this, so never send ID by default. Fallbacks: privacy@mylife.com, membersupport@mylife.com, mail to MyLife.com Inc., Attn: Privacy, 907 Westwood Blvd #359, Los Angeles CA 90024. Phone 888-704-1900 is reportedly unreliable. Re-check in 90 days. Live page returned 403 to me.

brokers.name: National Public Data (relaunched 2025)

brokers.notes: 403 on 2026-10-08 for /opt-out and /privacy-rights/. brokers.name: USA People Search

Stage 2 (Redact, 2026-05-27): first and last name, email, phone, street, city and state, with DOB optional. Required markers aren't shown; the site says to fill every applicable field, and no ZIP is documented. The Do-Not-Sell notice (live) is limited to comprehensive-privacy-law states and calls suppression a 'courtesy'. Phone: 800-248-1544. brokers.name: USPhoneBook
brokers.notes: Same company as FastPeopleSearch and its sister sites. Redact (May 2026): the form is at /removal; /opt-out is the older route. Form 1: 'I am', first, middle (optional) and last name, email, authorization box and reCAPTCHA, then 'Begin Removal Process'. The email from support@usphonebook.com ('Complete your usphonebook.com Privacy Request') often lands in spam and its link expires in 24h. Form 2: prefilled name, DOB (required only when no street address is given), phone, street, city, state, ZIP and email, plus reCAPTCHA. Removal takes 3 days or less. DeleteMe (2026-09-15) still describes the older phone-search, 'Remove Record' and email-link flow, which is stale. Phone fallback: (888) 747-4095. BADBOOL (Sept 2026) suggests support+optout@usphonebook.com if the form hangs. The site returns a Cloudflare 403 to automated fetch.

brokers.name: Veripages
brokers.notes: All veripages.com URLs return a Cloudflare challenge to me (even nonexistent paths). The receipt says 'within an hour'; the email says administrator approval up to 48h. Appeals: removal@veripages.com. Phone (844) 217-0978 is reportedly unanswered. brokers.name: VoterRecords.com

An email from support@voterrecords.com ('Verify Opt-Out Request') expires in under 24h, after which you see 'Record Opt-Out Successful'. The form says it removes house number, phone and email, but the 2026 FAQ names only the house number; name, age, party, street, city and voter status stay up. The site returns a 403 to automated fetch.

brokers.name: WeInform (We Inform LLC)
brokers.notes: Checked live 2026-10-08: same optOutLight template (name, full DOB, city, ZIP, state, email, then a confirmation link). Phone (855) 879-0159; registry contact support@weinform.org. The CA registry lists truthrecord.org under the same LLC; it runs a separate form.

brokers.name: Whitepages
brokers.notes: All whitepages.com and 411.com pages returned 403 / Cloudflare challenge to me. Only robots.txt loaded; it explicitly allows /suppress*, /suppression*, /optout and /opt-out. Flow (DeleteMe updated 2026-09-30, DuckDuckGo, Offlist, redact.dev Aug 2026): paste the listing URL, Next, confirm 'Remove Me', pick a reason, enter a phone number and tick the box, then 'Call now to verify' and key in the 4-digit code shown on screen. URL variants: DeleteMe uses /suppression_requests. Offlist, DuckDuckGo and Incogni use /suppression-requests. redact.dev reaches the same tool from /privacy/consumer-rights. Try another if one fails. 411.com is a Whitepages property: redact.dev says a 411.com listing URL works in this tool if you remove the 'www.'. Without a phone: email privacyrequest@whitepages.com (Optery, Offlist, redact.dev) with the listing URL, or use the support form at support.whitepages.com/hc/en-us/requests/new. The reply comes in about 2 business days, and support may ask for more information. Timing: typically under 24h, but Whitepages reportedly allows itself up to 15 days. Reverse-phone pages and duplicate profiles need their own requests. Re-listing after moves (NCOA data) is reported.

Box 2000, Conway, AR 72033. brokers.name: AnalyticsIQ

brokers.name: Cotality (formerly CoreLogic)
brokers.notes: corelogic.com redirects to cotality.com. brokers.name: Data Axle (formerly Infogroup)

brokers.name: Epsilon Data Management

brokers.name: Equifax (marketing / privacy opt-out)

brokers.name: Experian Marketing Services

brokers.name: InfutorData (formerly Verisk Marketing Solutions)

brokers.name: LexisNexis Risk Solutions

Box 105108, Atlanta, GA 30348-5108.

DELETION IS DIFFERENT: it requires government photo ID (or alternatives emailed to consumercare@liveramp.com), proof of residency in a regulated state, and an active email. Prefer opt-out. brokers.name: Pipl

The page says Pipl 'may need to reach out to you directly via email to verify your request' over the next few days. brokers.name: The Work Number (Equifax Workforce Solutions) data freeze
brokers.notes: THIS FORM REQUIRES A FULL SSN (marked required). It is a freeze of employment and income records, not a deletion; while it is on, verifiers cannot see the data, which can slow loan, job or benefit applications. The form says it 'may take up to 1 business day'. Follow-up messages come through Virtru with a one-time passcode sent to your email. Alternatives per theworknumber.com/employee-data-freeze (which redirects to employees.theworknumber.com): download the freeze form and mail it, or email it to TWNFreeze@equifax.com, or call 1-800-367-2884 (TTY 1-800-424-0253). Mail: Thomson Reuters - Westlaw and CLEAR Public Records, ATTN: Personal Information Request, 2900 Ames Crossing Rd Suite 100, Eagan, MN 55121, or email westlaw.privacypolicy@thomsonreuters.com.

brokers.name: Zeta Global

brokers.name: Apollo.io

Submit each current or former work email.

brokers.name: Clearbit (HubSpot Breeze Intelligence)

That is a DataGrail Privacy Request Center; its form config sits behind an authenticated API, so the fields could not be read. The policy lists privacy@hubspot.com and (866) 241-4820. HubSpot's partner FAQ says a delete or opt-out removes the person from the commercial database and tags them 'enrichment opt out' in customer CRMs. Already-delivered data is not recalled.

brokers.name: ContactOut
brokers.notes: In the live HTML, 'Verify your email' is a POST form to /optout/verify/send with one required email field and a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge, then 'Send verification link'. The page says details are used only to find your record and that the profile is deleted 'within the next 24 hours'. Older guides describe name plus profile URL plus CAPTCHA. The footer link is 'Do Not Sell My Info'. Only support@contactout.com appears in the privacy policy. Relisting has been reported, so recheck.

brokers.name: Dun & Bradstreet (incl. Hoovers contacts and Eyeota)
brokers.notes: Linked from D&B's live Personal Data page. Eyeota's Privacy Center (eyeota.com/privacy-center) links the SAME TrustArc form, and the form has an optional 'Eyeota Cookie ID' field, so one request covers D&B and Eyeota person-level data. Eyeota browser-cookie opt-outs may still need the cookie ID. Read from the live TrustArc form definition: REQUIRED fields are 'I am a' (data subject or agent), 'Resident of' (country, with US state), request type, name, email and a Disclaimer checkbox. Choose 'Opt Out of Marketing Communication(s) and/or Third Party Data Sharing in D&B Solutions', then tick the Third Party Sharing (Do not sell or share) box; 'Delete My Information' is also offered. Date of birth, phone, and company/DUNS details are OPTIONAL; don't send them. A required file upload appears only for authorised agents. The form uses CAPTCHA, and email verification is REQUIRED. D&B honours repeat requests for the same right at most once per 3 months. The page's general phone is (855) 540-1971. The California registry contact PrivacyOfficer@dnb.com is per a third party.

brokers.name: Lead411
brokers.notes: lead411.com returned 403 to curl and WebFetch on every page, and a Wayback snapshot (Oct 2, 2026) could not be fetched either. The flow comes from two 2026 guides that agree (DeleteMe, Sept 14, 2026; CrabClear, Aug 3, 2026). Pick the request type (delete / opt out), country and STATE, enter the work email, tick 'I Agree', pass the 'I'm not a robot' reCAPTCHA, then 'Get Code' to have a verification code emailed. Lead411 'tries to answer legitimate privacy requests within 30 days'. BBB complaints report non-responses, so keep a dated record. DeleteMe shows an obfuscated email; one guide lists support@lead411.io (unverified).

brokers.name: Lusha
brokers.notes: The official Request Removal page (https://www.lusha.com/privacy-center/request-removal/, linked from lushaprivacy.com) embeds this OneTrust form in an iframe. The sales/demo form seen earlier is a site-wide 'contact sales' popup on the same page, NOT the removal form; never fill it. The OneTrust form's request type is 'Data Deletion / Do Not Sell My Information'. Its config REQUIRES 'Why did you reach this page?' (a dropdown), Country of Residence, Email and preferred report delivery (Online or Mail). US state is optional, and NO NAME is asked. Email verification is ON, with Google reCAPTCHA. Lusha removes the record and suppression-lists it. No account needed. California phone route: 1-866-467-8688, service code 2001#. 2024 mean response for delete/opt-out: under 4 days.

brokers.name: People Data Labs
brokers.notes: The Privacy Center is a Transcend app (JS). Its published config and messages show a 'Delete my information' action for 'Consumer', an emailed verification link (requests cancel if it isn't clicked), and an acknowledgement that PDL keeps limited identifiers on a suppression list. Erasure has a 14-day window in which you can cancel. A phone number is OPTIONAL and triggers SMS verification; don't send it. The exact delete-form fields beyond email and residency were not rendered. The config sets privacy@peopledatalabs.com as the support and reply-to address. CORRECTION: https://www.peopledatalabs.com/opt-out-form now redirects to /do-not-sell-or-share, and that form REQUIRES Full Name, Email and 'State of origin' (with optional free text). It is not state-only, so the name/email minimisation benefit is gone; prefer deletion. PDL sells raw data to many downstream enrichment tools.

brokers.name: RocketReach
brokers.notes: Confirmed from the site's JS bundle: the 'Opt-Out of RocketReach / Remove Your Profile' view has one field, 'Email Address (We'll send a verification link here)'. It says no account is created and that it also serves as the 'sale' opt-out. The privacy policy links this page for both removal and Do Not Sell/Share, and lists privacy@rocketreach.co and (833) 212-3828. Per guides, the link arrives only if the email is in RocketReach's database, and it opens the actual removal step. No email does not prove there is no profile. Submit each current or former work email. Profiles can reappear after later crawls, so resubmit yearly.

brokers.name: Seamless.AI (Seamless Contacts Inc.)
brokers.notes: The live privacy policy (last updated Dec 14, 2025) links the 'Privacy Request Center' at https://preferences.seamless.ai/ for access, correct and delete and for state-law rights. That page returned 403 to curl and WebFetch, so the fields come from a July 28, 2026 guide: select country, then first name, last name, email, a phone or direct corporate line, and your relationship to Seamless.AI. The guide doesn't mark which are required; send phone only if the live form marks it required. Expect email confirmation and possible record matching. Per the policy, privacy@seamlessleads.com is for appeals and questions (Attention: Privacy Officer, Seamless Contacts, Inc., 7652 Sawmill Road, Suite 341, Dublin, OH 43016); the policy also lists (614) 665-0450. The Vermont registry lists an older form (login.seamless.ai/personalDataRequest) and email with 'Remove' in the subject. Company information is not removed.

brokers.name: UpLead
brokers.notes: In the live form HTML, the REQUIRED fields are Full Name, Contact Email (may be the same as or different from the email to remove), Jurisdiction (CCPA, VDPA, OCPA, TDPSA, GDPR or Other) and Request Type. Choose 'Delete my Information'; per UpLead that is also the opt-out. The email identifier and phone number to remove are optional, and so is the SMS-consent checkbox. Use email only to avoid sharing a phone; giving a phone triggers a 6-digit SMS code ('Verify Your Phone Number'). Cloudflare Turnstile/reCAPTCHA bot checks run on submit. Per UpLead's support article, verification is by email and/or SMS. Deletions are processed once ownership is confirmed; other requests within 30 days. The policy lists only support@uplead.com and (800) 493-4084.

brokers.name: ZoomInfo
brokers.notes: The URL is confirmed from ZoomInfo's live Trust Center ('Request Removal'). The form returned 403 to curl and WebFetch, so the flow comes from 2026 guides. Enter the WORK email ZoomInfo holds. Most guides say ZoomInfo emails a CODE to enter, not a link (a May 2026 guide says link). If the email doesn't match a profile, the form asks for more (full name, other emails, and so on); send only if asked. Removal also opts that profile out of sale/sharing; company data is not removed, and limited data is kept to prevent re-adding. Daniel's Law and similar covered persons can email stateremoval@zoominfo.com for expedited handling. The official notice also lists privacy@zoominfo.com, phone 833-901-0859, and ZoomInfo Technologies LLC, 330 W Columbia Way, Vancouver, WA 98660. Guides cite 24 hours for matched emails and up to 14-30 days otherwise. The official pages don't mention Datanyze, so assume it is not covered. Recheck about every 6 months.

references.name: Big-Ass Data Broker Opt-Out List (GitHub)
references.notes:
A community-maintained reference list, not an official source and not a request channel. It is a Markdown README on the 'master' branch; the raw file is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yaelwrites/Big-Ass-Data-Broker-Opt-Out-List/master/README.md. It says it was 'most recently updated on September 27, 2026'.

That update:
- removed Radaris and Rehold ('down due to a court order'), OpenDataUSA (registration expired) and Advanced Background Check
- added EveryJoe (opt-out: https://www.everyjoe.com/do-not-sell/)
- renamed United4Heritage to 'United Nations Public Administration Network'
It also says it 'is not always current'.

It lists 45 people-search entries, prioritised, with symbols for 'crucial', 'high priority', 'requires driver's license', 'must pick up a phone' and 'charges money'. It also points to DROP (it says '500+' brokers, now stale), OptOutPrescreen, DoNotCall.gov, optout.aboutads.info, Google Results about you, Bing's concern form (https://www.microsoft.com/en-ca/concern/bing) and the CFPB 2025 consumer reporting company list. Good for cross-checking people-search opt-out URLs found by other groups.

The CFPB 2025 PDF loads (HTTP 200): https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_consumer-reporting-companies_list_2025.pdf. This contradicts the earlier report of a 404.

references.name: California Data Broker Registry (CPPA), machine-readable CSV
references.notes:
A source of broker contact data, not an opt-out. It is the best machine-readable list for the tool.

Current CSV: https://cppa.ca.gov/data_broker_registry/registry.csv (page says Last Updated 7/29/2026). I downloaded it again: 603 data rows and 77 columns. Name, website, contact email, phone, postal address and the URL for exercising CA privacy rights are filled for all 603 rows; DBA is filled for 266.

Flag columns:
- collects minors' data, account logins, government ID numbers, citizenship/immigration, union membership, sexual orientation, gender identity, biometrics, precise geolocation, reproductive health
- sold or shared to foreign actors, the federal government, other states, law enforcement, or GenAI developers
- covered by FCRA, GLBA, IIPPA, CMIA or HIPAA
It also has request-handling metrics (headers say 2024).

Earlier years: /data_broker_registry/registry2025.csv (543 rows; a note row sits above the header), /data_broker_registry/registry2024.csv, and /data_broker_registry/complete-reg-data-brokers.csv (the 2020-2023 DOJ-era registry).

Gotcha, re-confirmed: the F5 WAF is inconsistent. A plain curl user agent got 200 once, then 403. A browser User-Agent plus Referer https://cppa.ca.gov/data_broker_registry/ returned 200 every time, for both registry.csv and registry2024.csv. The on-page table is filled by JavaScript, so scrapers see '0 data brokers registered'; use the CSV. Column layout changes between years, so map columns by header text.

references.name: Oregon Data Broker Registry (Division of Financial Regulation)
references.notes:
A list source, not an opt-out. Registration has been required since 2024-01-01 under HB 2052 (ORS 646A.593). The fee is $600 to register and $600 to renew. The DFR page does not cite HB 2008; HB 2008 (2025) amended the Oregon Consumer Privacy Act (a ban on selling precise geolocation and under-16 data from 2026-01-01), not the registry.

MACHINE-READABLE EXPORTS EXIST. They are linked as buttons on the DFR licence search page (https://www4.cbs.state.or.us/exs/all/mylicsearch/index.cfm?fuseaction=main.show_main&group_id=20&profession_id=28&profession_sub_id=28000) and are plain GET downloads:
(1) https://www4.cbs.state.or.us/ex/shared/downtemp/dfcs_db_optout.csv
- 390 brokers.
- Columns: licence no., name, DBA, update date, OPT OUT EMAIL (318 filled), OPT OUT STREET ADDRESS (239), OPT OUT PHONE (250), OPT OUT WEBSITE (374), additional website, other methods, and an opt-out narrative (all 390).
- Latest update date: 2026-09-24.
(2) https://www4.cbs.state.or.us/ex/shared/downtemp/dfcs_db_collected.csv
- 390 brokers.
- Shows which data types each broker collects, sells or licenses (name, address, DOB, place of birth, mother's maiden name, biometrics, SSN/government ID).
- Also shows whether consumers can opt out of all broker activity (325 Yes), whether an opt-out may be made BY PROXY or authorized agent (332 Yes), and opt-out scope for each data type.
The 'downtemp' path suggests the files are regenerated; the page says download files are updated daily.
(3) There is also a daily tab-delimited licensee file (licence no., firm, ABN, address, phone, start and renewal dates). It sits behind a POST form button, so I did not fetch it, because the rules forbid form submission.

Name search still works: https://ordcbs.mylicense.com/Verification/Search.aspx?facility=Y. The DFR licensing contact is dfr.ndp.licensing@dcbs.oregon.gov, 503-947-7300; this is an agency address, not a consumer opt-out channel.

Oregon residents have a deletion right under the OCPA, but there is no central mechanism. PRC/EFF (June 2025) found 475 brokers registered elsewhere but missing here.

references.name: Privacy Rights Clearinghouse Data Broker Database
references.notes:
A nonprofit merged view of 'five state registries': CA (CPPA and the legacy DOJ registry), Vermont, Texas and Oregon. It covers 750+ unique broker groups and links to nearly every broker's privacy policy. The data was gathered in early April 2025 (report dated 2025-06-20), so it is older than the CPPA 2026 CSV and the Oregon CSVs.

The interactive view is an embedded Tableau Public dashboard. I found no CSV or JSON download link on the page. It is most useful for spotting brokers registered in some states but not others; as of April 2025, 291 were missing in CA, 524 in TX, 475 in OR and 309 in VT. For current contact details, use the state CSVs directly (CA registry.csv, Oregon dfcs_db_optout.csv).

references.name: Texas Data Broker Registry (Secretary of State)
references.notes:
A list source, not an opt-out. Searchable registry: https://texas-sos.appianportalsgov.com/data-broker-registry. It is an Appian JavaScript app; a plain fetch returns a 2.5 KB shell. I found no CSV or bulk export, and the SOS page mentions none.

Brokers pay $300 to register and $300 a year to renew. The SOS page says it 'does not have the authority' to regulate, investigate or enforce; enforcement sits with the Attorney General under the statute. The SOS page lists broker duties: a conspicuous website notice (510.004) and an information security program (510.007).

Texas residents have a deletion right under the TDPSA but must file it broker by broker; there is no central mechanism.

The PRC/EFF letter (June 2025) counted 226 brokers registered in Texas and 524 registered elsewhere but missing here.

Statute numbering conflicts. The SOS page cites Bus. & Com. Code ch. 510, while the 2023 enactment (SB 2105) created ch. 509. One third-party source says it was redesignated as 510 effective 2025-09-01; I could not confirm this on the official statutes site, which is a JS app.

references.name: Vermont Data Broker Registry (Secretary of State)
references.notes:
A list source, not an opt-out. Brokers register every January (Jan 1-31).

Public search: https://bizfilings.vermont.gov/databrokersearch/Search. It returned HTTP 200 to me, but it is an Angular app shell, so a plain fetch sees no records. The sos.vermont.gov page returned 403 to curl but loaded through WebFetch. The old URL /corporations/other-services/data-brokers/ is a 404.

Act 138 (H.211), signed 2026-06-16. I read the enacted text on legislature.vermont.gov.
- Sec. 1, effective 2027-01-01:
  - The registration fee rises from $100 to $900, and brokers must post a $20,000 bond.
  - Brokers must disclose more, including a URL where consumers can request deletion 'if the data broker permits deletion', and their opt-out methods, including whether an authorized agent may opt out for you.
  - The Secretary of State must publish a publicly accessible page with a DOWNLOADABLE SPREADSHEET of registered brokers and their registration information. This will be the machine-readable source for the tool once it exists.
  - The Act creates NO general consumer right to delete and NO state deletion portal.
- Sec. 2, effective 2026-07-01: only a feasibility STUDY of an accessible deletion mechanism, with an interim report due 2027-12-01 and a final report due 2028-12-01.
Hunton (June 2026) describes a new consumer deletion right with 30-day processing. That does not match the enacted text; it likely reflects an earlier draft.

The reported 'Bulk Database Download' in the logged-in bizfilings portal remains unverified. Privacy Rights Clearinghouse (data from April 2025) found 309 brokers registered in other states but missing here.
